name: Tsukishima
description: Tsukishima and Tsukuda from open data, lit by the real sun: Monja Street's shops, Tsukuda's fishing village by the Sumida with its moat and shrine, and Kachidoki Bridge's arches.

佃小橋.note: the deck under the vermilion railings city.py draws

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped, and the shared trees have no ginkgo or cherry, so the mix stands in: elms for the zelkovas, plane trees for the street planes and the riverside's cherries. A guess, not a survey.

areas.name: Ishikawajima Park
areas.note: Cherries along the Sumida's terrace at the tip of Tsukudajima.

tour.title: Tsukishima, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Monja Street
tour.text: About seventy monjayaki shops along Nishinaka-dori, lit after dark. The signs here are typical of the street, not its real shops'.

tour.title: Kachidoki Bridge
tour.text: 1940: two tied arches either side of a bascule that last opened in 1970, over the Sumida's mouth.

sources.landmarks: Kachidoki Bridge (1940; Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Kachidoki Bridge Museum: 246 m, arches of 86 m, bascule of 44 m) on OpenStreetMap's centre lines; the river bridges on OpenStreetMap's outlines and lines, their colours from photographs; Tsukuda Kobashi and Sumiyoshi Shrine's torii from photographs. Monja Street's signs are indicative: typical trades, no real shops' signs.

game.title: Tsukishima on Foot
game.blurb: Walk Tsukishima under the real sun: down Monja Street for monjayaki, through Tsukuda's old fishing village by its moat and shrine, and along the Sumida to Kachidoki Bridge.

areas.name: 月島
areas.note: Monja Street, on land made from the bay in 1892

areas.name: 築地
areas.note: The outer market across the river

travel.name: Monja Street もんじゃストリート
Kachidoki Bridge, the east end 勝鬨橋

npcs.name: Haru 春
npcs.role: Monja shop owner もんじゃ屋
idle: Monja: flour, water, dashi, cabbage. Make a bank of the cabbage and pour the batter in the middle. Don't rush it.
My mother's shop, and her mother's sweet shop before that. Children bought monja for five yen. {time}.

npcs.name: Kiyoshi 清
idle: Tsukudani: little fish boiled down in soy and sugar until they keep for months. The fishermen of Tsukuda made it first, in Edo's time.
The moat out there was where the boats tied up. Now it's for the shrine's poles, sunk in the mud between festivals. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Nao 奈央
idle: Kachidoki Bridge opened five times a day once, for twenty minutes. The last time was 1970.
The motors are still inside the piers. You can see them on a tour.

npcs.name: Riku 陸
idle: The terrace runs along the Sumida all the way to Kachidoki Bridge. Best at sunset, with the towers lit across the river.
Everybody runs here, then eats monja. That's the deal.

quests.title: Tsukishima
talk: Welcome to Tsukishima! This island was made from the bay in 1892, for factories. Now it's made of monja.
Sit down later. First go and see Tsukuda, the old village at the top of the island. Kiyoshi makes tsukudani there.

quests.title: Tsukuda
talk: Tsukuda: the fishermen came from Osaka in 1590, invited by the shogun. Their shrine is still here.
Go and look at it, by the river. Then follow the terrace down to the bridge; Riku runs there every evening.

steps.text: Find Riku on the river terrace

quests.title: The terrace
talk: Down the river, Kachidoki Bridge: the arches, and the middle that used to open.
Nao at the bridge museum will tell you how it worked.

quests.title: Kachidoki Bridge
talk: Look at the bridge from the bank: two arches, and the bascule between them.
Then go back to Monja Street. Haru will have the plate hot.
